description:
FILED s452ab (Opus, round 11 agent AB) from the #721 probes.  PRE-EXISTING on
main 0dd7434 (verified by running the repro against a 0dd7434 worktree --
identical output), and #721 did NOT change it.

A sub whose WHOLE body is the parameter unpack returns nothing:

    sub bar { my ($x) = @_ }
    my @r = bar(9); my $s = bar(9);
        perl: list 1 element (9), scalar 1     (the RHS element count)
        PCL:  list 0 elements,    scalar undef

WHY: `Pl::Parser2::_lower_sub_inner`'s signature fast path (#3) recognises a
LEADING `my (LIST) = @_` and lowers it to `p-raw-params`, which binds the
names raw and DROPS the assignment form entirely.  When the unpack was the
only statement the body is then `(block nil)` -- no value.  The sibling
shift-coalescing path already handles exactly this case: it sets
`$tail_param` when the run consumed the whole body, so `sub f { my $x =
shift }` returns $x.  The `my (LIST) = @_` path has no equivalent.

The correct tail value is #721's rule: LIST context -> the parameter list,
SCALAR/void -> the number of arguments.  The obstacle measured here: inside
`p-raw-params` the argument count is NOT available -- the macro rebinds
`%_args` and POPs it, and the guard for taking this path is precisely that
the body never mentions `@_`, so no `@_` is bound.  So the fix needs the
entry-time length captured (e.g. bind it in the macro before the pops, or
emit the tail value in the enclosing p-sub where `%_args` is still whole),
which is why this was filed rather than done inside #721.

The BOXED convention's twin of the same shape (`sub ($x) {}` from a
v1-lowered SIGNATURE, whose body is empty so the synthesized `my ($x) = @_`
is the tail) is a DIFFERENT bug and is #752.

BAR: the two rows above vs perl; `sub f { my ($a,$b) = @_ }` in both
contexts with 1, 2 and 3 arguments; the shift-coalesced twin unchanged; a
body that DOES have statements unchanged (emission A/B -- this shape is
common, so read every diff); guard rows in Pl/t/aassign-01.t.
subject: sub f { my ($x) = @_ } returns NOTHING -- the p-raw-params fast path drops the unpack's statement value
